en.title: Typing Time on a Single-Row Keyboard
en.description:
Each of the 26 lowercase letters appears exactly once on the keyboard. The finger starts at index 0, and each move takes time equal to the absolute difference of the indices. Type word in order and find the total movement time. The source example's keyboard was missing z; this site appends z at the end, which does not change the time for cba.

The standard input/output format was compiled by CSWork; value ranges marked "this site" are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: The first line is a permutation of the 26 lowercase letters; the second line is word, which on this site has length 1..100000 and contains only lowercase letters.
en.output: Output the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: moving from a to c takes 2, then to b takes 1 and to a takes 1, for a total of 4. Example 2: typing a first requires no movement, then moving to z takes 25, for a total of 25. Example 3: z is at index 0, so no movement is needed and the answer is 0.
hints: Precompute the position of each letter, then add up the distance from the previous position for each character in order.
